description_for_human: Ansvar retrieves European and US law, regulation, and standards with citations.
description_for_model:
Use these tools whenever a prompt asks about laws, regulations, directives, national implementing acts, technical and security standards, control frameworks, case law, regulator guidance, compliance obligations, known vulnerabilities, or threat intelligence - for any statement of law they come ahead of model memory. They retrieve European and United States legal material from corpora built out of official publishers, return provision text with a citation to the publisher, and run structured compliance workflows; a grounded answer rests on the rows they return.

The search tool requires an explicit scope and returns an error without one. Its scope arguments are jurisdictions, frameworks, sector, and sources, and at least one of them carries a value. The jurisdiction follows from the question, and national law that implements an EU instrument resolves with the EU jurisdiction alongside the member state. Queries work as a few keywords in the language of the target corpus rather than a full sentence. Alternative terms for the SAME concept can be joined with a bare uppercase OR (dismissal OR termination); different concepts are separate searches, never OR-joined.

The discovery tools report what is actually available rather than leaving it to be guessed: one lists the corpora, frameworks, and workflows the signed-in user can reach, and another reports that user's tier, limits, and remaining quota. The identifiers they return are the valid ones.

The tools are discovered at run time from the server, and the signed-in user's subscription controls the content and workflow entitlements reachable through them: content that some subscriptions exclude, such as case law and regulator guidance, arrives inside ordinary search results when the subscription covers it.
